title: Evaluating the Impact of Fertilizer Subsidy on Crop Yields

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID). We compare changes in log yields (y) over time between subsidized (treated = 1) and non-subsidized (treated = 0) farmers before and after the subsidy (post = 1).
- Why: The policy impacts only the treated group in the post period; DID nets out time-invariant differences between groups and common shocks over time.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the subsidy, treated and control groups would have experienced the same change in y over time.
  - No spillovers/contamination between groups.
  - Stable composition and no differential measurement changes across periods.
  - No anticipatory behavior affecting the pre period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code for DID with robustness checks

# 0) Packages
need_pkgs <- c("sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in need_pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s50_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic sanity checks and coercions
df$treated <- as.integer(df$treated)
df$post    <- as.integer(df$post)
df$period  <- as.integer(df$period)
# Keep a numeric cluster id; also keep a factor for FE if panel
df$unit_id_num <- as.integer(df$unit_id)
df$unit_id_fac <- as.factor(df$unit_id)

# Detect whether we have a panel (same unit_id appearing in multiple periods)
panel_by_unit <- any(duplicated(df$unit_id_num))

cat("Data summary:\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Unique units:", length(unique(df$unit_id_num)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", length(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Panel structure (repeated unit_ids):", panel_by_unit, "\n\n")

# 2) Main DID specification
# If panel: include unit and period FE; key regressor is treated:post
# If repeated cross-sections: standard DID with treated + post + interaction
if (panel_by_unit) {
  formula_main <- y ~ treated:post + factor(unit_id_num) + factor(period)
} else {
  formula_main <- y ~ treated + post + treated:post
}

mod_main <- lm(formula_main, data = df)

# Robust variance: cluster by unit if panel; otherwise HC1
if (panel_by_unit) {
  vcov_main <- sandwich::vcovCL(mod_main, cluster = ~ unit_id_num, type = "HC1")
} else {
  vcov_main <- sandwich::vcovHC(mod_main, type = "HC1")
}

ct_main <- coeftest(mod_main, vcov. = vcov_main)

# Extract the ATT (interaction) coefficient robustly by name
att_names <- intersect(rownames(ct_main), c("treated:post", "post:treated", "treat_x_post"))
if (length(att_names) == 0) {
  stop("Could not find the DID interaction term in the model coefficients.")
}
att_name <- att_names[1]
att_est  <- as.numeric(ct_main[att_name, "Estimate"])
att_se   <- as.numeric(ct_main[att_name, "Std. Error"])
att_t    <- as.numeric(ct_main[att_name, "t value"])
att_p    <- as.numeric(ct_main[att_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])

# 95% CI using normal approximation
z_crit <- 1.96
ci_low <- att_est - z_crit * att_se
ci_high <- att_est + z_crit * att_se

cat("Main DID estimate (treated x post):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-value = %.4g\n\n",
            att_est, att_se, ci_low, ci_high, att_p))

# 3) Robustness Check A: Use pre-computed interaction (treat_x_post)
if (panel_by_unit) {
  formula_rbA <- y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id_num) + factor(period)
  mod_rbA <- lm(formula_rbA, data = df)
  vcov_rbA <- sandwich::vcovCL(mod_rbA, cluster = ~ unit_id_num, type = "HC1")
} else {
  formula_rbA <- y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post
  mod_rbA <- lm(formula_rbA, data = df)
  vcov_rbA <- sandwich::vcovHC(mod_rbA, type = "HC1")
}
ct_rbA <- coeftest(mod_rbA, vcov. = vcov_rbA)

if ("treat_x_post" %in% rownames(ct_rbA)) {
  est_rbA <- as.numeric(ct_rbA["treat_x_post", "Estimate"])
  se_rbA  <- as.numeric(ct_rbA["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"])
  p_rbA   <- as.numeric(ct_rbA["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"])
  ciA_lo  <- est_rbA - z_crit * se_rbA
  ciA_hi  <- est_rbA + z_crit * se_rbA
  cat("Robustness A (using treat_x_post explicitly):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Coef = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-value = %.4g\n\n",
              est_rbA, se_rbA, ciA_lo, ciA_hi, p_rbA))
} else {
  cat("Robustness A: treat_x_post coefficient not found (possibly collinear).\n\n")
}

# 4) Robustness Check B: Manual Difference-in-Differences from cell means
agg <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = function(x) c(mean = mean(x), var = var(x), n = length(x)))
# Unpack aggregated list-columns
agg_mean <- sapply(agg$y, function(z) z["mean"])
agg_var  <- sapply(agg$y, function(z) z["var"])
agg_n    <- sapply(agg$y, function(z) z["n"])
agg2 <- data.frame(treated = agg$treated, post = agg$post,
                   mean = as.numeric(agg_mean),
                   var = as.numeric(agg_var),
                   n = as.numeric(agg_n))

get_cell <- function(t, p, col = "mean") {
  vals <- agg2[agg2$treated == t & agg2$post == p, col]
  if (length(vals) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  return(vals[1])
}

m11 <- get_cell(1,1,"mean"); m10 <- get_cell(1,0,"mean"); m01 <- get_cell(0,1,"mean"); m00 <- get_cell(0,0,"mean")
v11 <- get_cell(1,1,"var");  v10 <- get_cell(1,0,"var");  v01 <- get_cell(0,1,"var");  v00 <- get_cell(0,0,"var")
n11 <- get_cell(1,1,"n");    n10 <- get_cell(1,0,"n");    n01 <- get_cell(0,1,"n");    n00 <- get_cell(0,0,"n")

if (all(!is.na(c(m11, m10, m01, m00)))) {
  did_manual <- (m11 - m10) - (m01 - m00)
  # Naive SE for DID using within-cell variances (assuming independence)
  se_manual <- NA_real_
  if (all(!is.na(c(v11, v10, v01, v00, n11, n10, n01, n00))) && all(c(n11,n10,n01,n00) > 1)) {
    var_did <- v11/n11 + v10/n10 + v01/n01 + v00/n00
    se_manual <- sqrt(var_did)
  }
  cat("Robustness B (manual DID from group-time means):\n")
  if (is.na(se_manual)) {
    cat(sprintf("  DID (no SE computed) = %.4f\n\n", did_manual))
  } else {
    ciB_lo <- did_manual - z_crit * se_manual
    ciB_hi <- did_manual + z_crit * se_manual
    cat(sprintf("  DID = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
                did_manual, se_manual, ciB_lo, ciB_hi))
  }
} else {
  cat("Robustness B: Not all four group-time cells observed; manual DID not computed.\n\n")
}

# 5) Optional: First-difference check if bona fide two-period panel for most units
if (panel_by_unit && length(unique(df$period)) == 2) {
  # Keep only units observed in both periods
  tab_counts <- table(df$unit_id_num)
  keep_ids <- as.integer(names(tab_counts[tab_counts == 2]))
  df_both <- df[df$unit_id_num %in% keep_ids, ]
  # Reshape to compute delta y = y_post - y_pre per unit
  # Identify post period as max(period)
  post_val <- max(df_both$period, na.rm = TRUE)
  pre_val  <- min(df_both$period, na.rm = TRUE)

  y_pre  <- df_both[df_both$period == pre_val, c("unit_id_num","y","treated")]
  y_post <- df_both[df_both$period == post_val, c("unit_id_num","y","treated")]
  names(y_pre)[2]  <- "y_pre"
  names(y_post)[2] <- "y_post"

  df_wide <- merge(y_pre, y_post, by = c("unit_id_num","treated"), all = FALSE)
  df_wide$dy <- df_wide$y_post - df_wide$y_pre

  mod_fd <- lm(dy ~ treated, data = df_wide)
  vcov_fd <- sandwich::vcovHC(mod_fd, type = "HC1")
  ct_fd <- coeftest(mod_fd, vcov. = vcov_fd)

  if ("treated" %in% rownames(ct_fd)) {
    est_fd <- as.numeric(ct_fd["treated","Estimate"])
    se_fd  <- as.numeric(ct_fd["treated","Std. Error"])
    p_fd   <- as.numeric(ct_fd["treated","Pr(>|t|)"])
    ci_fd_lo <- est_fd - z_crit * se_fd
    ci_fd_hi <- est_fd + z_crit * se_fd
    cat("Robustness C (first-difference estimator on two-period panel):\n")
    cat(sprintf("  Coef = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p-value = %.4g\n",
                est_fd, se_fd, ci_fd_lo, ci_fd_hi, p_fd))
  } else {
    cat("Robustness C: treated coefficient not found in FD model.\n")
  }
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Fertilizer subsidies reduce input costs and should raise application rates, increasing yields.
- Magnitude: For log yields, an ATT of about 0.05–0.15 (≈5–15%) is plausible; around 0.10 (≈10%) is a reasonable benchmark given typical elasticities and agronomic responses for smallholders when constraints are relaxed.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log crop yields over time between treated and untreated units.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy program significantly increased crop yields.
